questions.question: How does Tomek know it will be hot that morning?
answers: Only from the TV forecast
From his experience of the forest — he recognises drought without a thermometer
From tourists on the bus
From a running app
questions.explanation: His father taught him to read the forest by looking, not from books; Tomek recognises drought without a thermometer.

questions.question: What does the father tell Tomek about the drought?
answers: That it's normal spring weather
That it is no longer a normal drought but a change, and he doesn't know how long the trees will hold out
That it's enough to water the forest with a garden hose
That pines are resistant to everything
questions.explanation: The father says every year it gets worse and it is no longer a normal drought but a change.

questions.question: Why does the idea of planting different trees prove difficult?
answers: Because pines have grown on the sands of the Bory for centuries
Because the forest is protected by building regulations
Because Tomek doesn't like plants
Because there's no room for trees
questions.explanation: The father says these are sands and pine has grown here for centuries; if it can't make it, he doesn't know what can.

questions.question: What happens in the epilogue in 2029?
answers: The forest is completely cut down
A water retention programme and adaptation measures appear
Tomek abandons his work in the forest
The drought ends immediately
questions.explanation: The epilogue describes the programme for rebuilding retention, new reservoirs and the actions of cities and farmers.

questions.question: What is the characters' attitude at the end of the story?
answers: Pessimism without action
Awareness of the difficulties, but the feeling that trying makes sense
Belief that the problem has been solved
Giving up on ecology
questions.explanation: The ending says that if something changes now, maybe it will be possible to stop what is inevitable — and if not, at least they tried.
